audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings tell the player Riftwalk lets him 'sidestep' Depth Charge or 'leave his Depth Charge's path' — spikes[1].text, content.mid and whys[4]. Depth Charge chases its target. There is no path to leave.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'fires a shockwave into the earth that chases an opponent... when it reaches the opponent, the shockwave erupts, knocking his target into the air and stunning them.' A Kassadin who blinks sideways expecting to dodge it gets knocked up mid-reposition, which is exactly the moment Nautilus's team wants. The blink is worth saving for after it lands, not for beating it.
audit.corrected: Corrected in spikes[1].text, whys[4], content.mid, wants.foe[2], phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Staggering Blow's root is treated as part of a chain Kassadin 'has no escape from'. Riftwalk is a blink, and roots do not disable blinks.
audit.why: Pre-6 the page is right for the wrong reason — he has no escape because he has no ultimate. Post-6 the reason stops being true, and the page never updates: his passive root pins the feet and Riftwalk still fires. That distinction is what separates a survivable hook from a death, and only Depth Charge's knock-up actually locks the blink out.
audit.corrected: Written into spikes[1].text, whys[4], phases[4].why, breakdown.mid and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dredge Line's range is 1150 against Null Sphere's 650, and it is on 14/13/12/11/10s. None of those numbers appear anywhere on the page.
audit.why: 'Don't walk into hook range to last-hit' is unactionable without knowing hook range is 500 units further than his own. The 14 seconds is also the entire green-light system the page keeps gesturing at without printing.
audit.corrected: Added to tldr, spikes[0].text, wants.you[0], content.early, phases[0].why, phases[3].why, tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[1].d and All-In Windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late and whys[6] describe Nautilus as 'immobile apart from one telegraphed hook'. Dredge Line colliding with TERRAIN pulls Nautilus to the wall instead.
audit.why: Beside any wall — which in top lane is most of the map — he has a repositioning tool, so the plan of blinking in and killing the carry 'before he can reposition' has a hole in it exactly where the terrain is.
audit.corrected: Stated in spikes[3].text, content.late and whys[6].

audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating reads 7/10 and both rating lines say 'Tricky matchup', while full.diff reads EVEN and the packet records 49.12% over 57 games — the largest and flattest sample in this slice.
audit.why: A 49.12% lane over 57 games is the definition of even. A 7/10 tells the player to concede stages he does not have to.
audit.corrected: diffRating 7/10 to 5/10 and both rating lines reworded to 'Even matchup', matching diff=EVEN. Nautilus's carry threat left at 7.5/10 — the hook-to-Depth-Charge chain really is that punishing when it lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0] to [6] are the generic Kassadin boilerplate. Not one of them names Dredge Line's range, Riptide's cooldown, or what changes at 6 beyond 'you're mobile at last'.
audit.why: The stages in this lane are defined by exactly two thresholds — the hook's 14 seconds and level 6 — and the chart describes neither.
audit.corrected: phases[0] through [4] and phases[6] rewritten around the real numbers and the root-versus-blink distinction.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d offers 'the fifteen-second invitation' for a spent Dredge Line, and breakdown.cooldowns prints no number at all.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5 — the fifteen is close at rank 1 and four seconds wrong by rank 5, which is precisely the window a Kassadin dies in. Riptide at 7s to 5 is the other cooldown that decides an extended trade and it is never mentioned.
audit.corrected: Real numbers in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, tradeGood, phases[1].why and All-In Windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Void Stone appears as '15% magic reduction' in spikes[2], wants.you[1], content.mid and whys[5]; phases[2].why carries the 'E only charges when spells fly' boilerplate; breakdown.late says 'Q-silence the counterplay'.
audit.why: Void Stone has been 10% since V11.24, Force Pulse stopped being charge-gated in V12.23 (it is a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown that nearby casts shorten by a second each), and Null Sphere has never had a silence in its current form.
audit.corrected: 15% set to 10% in all four places; phases[2].why moved to the cooldown model; the silence replaced with the shield.

edits.before: Nautilus's whole threat before 6 is a single point of failure: Dredge Line. The hook drags you to him, his passive roots you on the first auto that follows, and Riptide's waves chunk you while you're stuck — and you have no Riftwalk yet to answer any of it. Don't walk into hook range to last-hit when his Q is up; farm with Null Sphere from max range and concede a little CS rather than eat a full combo. You out-trade him at nothing here, so play around his Q cooldown and never get pinned against the wave where the hook is unmissable.
edits.after: Nautilus's whole threat before 6 is a single point of failure: Dredge Line. It reaches 1150 against your 650, drags you to him, his passive roots you on the first auto that follows, and Riptide's waves chunk you while you're stuck — and you have no Riftwalk yet to answer any of it. Don't walk inside 1150 to last-hit while his Q is up; farm with Null Sphere from max range and concede a little CS rather than eat a full combo. Play around a 14-second hook and never get pinned against the wave where it cannot miss.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay a weather-the-storm phase — Nether Blade's mana restore keeps you topped up and a maxed Null Sphere lets you farm under tower, but you still fight only on his terms, so don't contest unless his Q is down. Level 6 changes the math: Riftwalk gives you a blink to sidestep a committed hook, leave the line of his Depth Charge, and escape the gank his CC enables. Then Rod of Ages comes online — the health, mana, and your Q shield, stacked on your innate 15% magic reduction, turn his combo from lethal to survivable, and the lane settles to even.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay a weather-the-storm phase — Nether Blade's mana restore keeps you topped up and a maxed Null Sphere lets you farm under tower, but you fight only on his terms, so don't contest unless his Q is down. Level 6 changes the math: Riftwalk is a blink, so his passive root no longer holds you — though Depth Charge chases and cannot be dodged, only pre-empted. Then Rod of Ages lands: health, mana and the Q shield on top of Void Stone's 10% turn his combo from lethal to survivable, and the lane settles to even.

edits.before: This is the lane I play for. With 2+ items and Riftwalk ramping its damage on each recast, I blink onto the squishiest target, burst it, and blink out before Nautilus — immobile apart from one telegraphed hook — can even reposition to throw Dredge Line at me. His only answer is catching me the instant I land, with a pre-aimed hook or a Depth Charge into the rest of his team, so I never blink into a waiting Nautilus; I pick the angle, kill the carry, and Riftwalk clear. A lone Nautilus has no tool that pins me anymore.
edits.after: This is the lane I play for. With 2+ items and Riftwalk ramping its damage on each recast, I blink onto the squishiest target, burst it, and blink out before Nautilus can throw Dredge Line at me — though beside a wall he can hook the terrain and pull himself back into it, so he is not as stranded as he looks. His real answer is catching me the instant I land, with a pre-aimed hook or a Depth Charge that chases rather than aims. So I never blink into a waiting Nautilus; I pick the angle, kill the carry, and Riftwalk clear.

notes: The Depth Charge correction is the one that matters most here: three separate strings told the player to sidestep or leave the path of an ability that chases its target, and a Kassadin who blinks laterally to dodge it is knocked up mid-blink. Riot's own text is unambiguous. CHART: content win[] and full phases[] read Nautilus/Nautilus/Nautilus/Nautilus/Skill/Skill/Kassadin, which matches the packet levelChart closely enough (the packet has Skill at level 1 and Skill at first item) and is consistent with a flat 49.12% over 57 games. Left alone. CHAMPION-WIDE, VERIFIED ON THE WIKI: Void Stone is 10% magic damage reduction, not 15% (V11.24) — same character count, so the fix applies cleanly anywhere '15%' appears across the champion; and Force Pulse has not been charge-gated since V12.23, so the phases[2].why boilerplate 'E only charges when spells fly' is wrong on all 71 Kassadin matchups. The kit file reproduces Riot's pre-rework tooltip, so both will regenerate unless fixed at the source. _missing-interactions.json's entry for this matchup ('Nautilus can cancel your Null Sphere with Staggering Blow, Dredge Line, Depth Charge') is inverted — Null Sphere is not a channel, it interrupts them — and was not written into any string.
